title: Listening to Affected Communities to Define Extreme Speech: Dataset and Experiments

bias_targets.methodology: Using LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) feature attribution to extract top-contributing words, revealing that the model disproportionately relies on specific ethnic group names (e.g., 'Rohingyas', 'Kikuyu', 'Luo') to classify text as extreme speech.
Applying LIME to model predictions to demonstrate an over-reliance on religious identity terms (e.g., 'Muslims', 'Islam', 'Moslems') as spurious indicators of extreme speech.

Using LIME to show that models heavily weight gendered terms and sexual orientation/gender identity slurs (e.g., 'traveco', a Brazilian Portuguese term for cross-dresser/trans women) rather than relying on the actual harmful context of the speech.
Analyzing top-contributing words via LIME to find that the model uses the names of political figures and parties (e.g., 'Merkel', 'Grünen') as strong predictive features for derogatory speech.
